text:
maya: Quick thread on "evaporation" semantics for the credits/billing pipeline. Need a compact contract: when does a provisional token evaporate (ignored) vs remain recoverable as a late arrival? Thinking soft vs hard windows.
samir: Good call. Are we distinguishing runtime-provisional events (fast path) from post-join compact events (authoritative)?
maya: Yes 100%. Fast path should be provisional and reconcilable. Compact path should be the canonical source once compacted/merged.
nora: We should define two parameters: soft_window (minutes) where we try to reconcile late compact events into provisional claims, and hard_cutoff where provisional entries are tombstoned and future compact events only create new canonical entries (with adjustments).
liam: Implementation idea: envelope adds "evaporate_at" timestamp (epoch ms) and a provenance pointer. Ingest keeps provisional rows until evaporate_at. Reconciler looks for compact matches before evaporate_at and upgrades the provisional to canonical. After evaporate_at we emit an "evaporated" audit and mark provisional tombstoned.
ops-carol: Ops note: we already have quota-grace windows per-tenant. Exposing billing-level soft_window/hard_cutoff per-tenant is doable but increases config surface. Recommend global defaults + tenant overrides for enterprise.
finance-ella: From finance: whatever we choose, it must be visible in billing docs and invoices. Tenants must be able to opt into deterministic behavior for audits.
samir: Tradeoffs: longer soft_window reduces double-charges but increases memory/retention for provisional store and delays near-real-time billing. Short windows improve apparent throughput but risk late corrections.
liam: Also: idempotency/dedupe is critical. Suggest dedupe_key := sha256(tenant|fingerprint|source|event_seq|parent_trace_id?). Use same key in both provisional and compact writes so reconciler can detect duplicates.
nora: Parent_trace_id helps with stitched requests (runtime splits). If runtime splits a logical request across shards, include parent_trace_id and sub_index. Ingest uses parent_trace_id to coalesce attribution before dedupe/hashing. Keep subfields optional to avoid cardinality bloat.
maya: Example envelope snippet (informal):
```
{
  "tenant": "acme",
  "fingerprint": "fp-..",
  "source": "runtime-v1",
  "event_seq": 12345,
  "parent_trace_id": "p-abc-1",
  "evaporate_at": 1680000000000,
  "model_id": "rwd-7b",
  "route": "/chat",
  "tokens": {"prompt": 24, "completion": 48}
}
```
Keep schema minimal; avoid adding lots of optional nested blobs.
ops-carol: Audit retention cost question: long tail of tombstone/audit events is expensive. Proposal: full detailed audit retained 90d default, aggregated ballots (daily summaries) 2y. Tenants with compliance needs can flag longer retention.
finance-ella: Agreed. Also require an immutable "audit-ballot" blob that contains only references/proofs (hashes) so we can store compact proofs cheaply.
samir: Backfill & migrations: if we change soft_window/hard_cutoff semantics later, do NOT rewrite historical invoices. Instead, produce reconciliation-candidates stream with proposed adjustments and require manual approval to apply. No automatic backdated billing adjustments.
liam: Implementation detail: reconciler job (billing-keeper) runs every N seconds (configurable). If soft_window increases, reconciler frequency and checkpointing need tuning to avoid long-running scans. infra-bot: note created: job "billing-keeper" cron=2m default.

liam: Tombstone/audit events should include reason tags: {reason: evaporated|merged|deduped|reconciled}, pointer to canonical_id, and reconciler_run_id. That gives traceability for ops/finance.
nora: For dedupe we must consider replayed events from client/library restarts. Keep a compact idempotency index with TTL > max(soft_window, consumer_lag). Use RocksDB/redis with eviction policy tuned to window size.
maya: Security: provenance pointers can leak internal ids. Mask/shorten them before showing to customers in the audit UI; internal logs retain raw pointers for compliance.
ops-carol: Emergency rollback path: use corrective adjustment entries appended to ledger (negative charges), do not mutate original rows. Ops UI must show candidate adjustments and allow 2-person approval for > $threshold.
nora: Also add an "adjustment_candidate" stream that reconciler writes when encountering ambiguous matches. Operators review and either approve (emit adjustment) or reject (leave invoice as-is and flag upstream.
liam: Edge case: compaction frontier 12: compact jobs can merge events across shard boundaries. Need to ensure reconciler uses stable compact keys (e.g., canonical_fingerprint) emitted by compactor so matches are deterministic.
samir: Operational alerting: create alerts for unusual rates of "evaporated" audits or high reconciliation candidate backlog. Those indicate regressions in runtime emission or compaction.

infra-bot: alert rule created: "evaporation-spike" -> page eng-platform if > 50/min for 5m.

maya: Action items: 1) Samir: PR with envelope schema + validator rules (include evaperate_at, optional parent_trace_id, model/route minimal tags). 2) Liam: prototype dedupe store and reconciler run in sandbox, include audit events. 3) Nora: draft backfill/adjustment policy doc for legal/finance review. 4) Ops-Carol: wireframe approval UI + ops playbook for adjustments. 5) Finance-Ella: list reporting/audit needs for invoices and export schemas.
samir: I'll do the schema PR by EOD tomorrow (will include example JSON schema + compact validator).
liam: I'll push a small sandbox spike showing dedupe_key behaviour and tombstone audit emission later this week.
nora: I'll draft policy and ping legal/finance in the PR.
ops-carol: I'll mockup UI flows and add approval gating notes.
finance-ella: I'll compile invoice visibility reqs and expected fields.

maya: Thanks team. If anyone thinks of additional failure modes drop them here. Key remaining question: what's sensible default for soft_window/hard_cutoff? My gut: soft_window=5m, hard_cutoff=24h. Open to empirical tuning.
liam: 5m soft_window is a good starting point. We can telemetry it and make per-tenant overrides later.
nora: +1. Let's start conservative and measure.
maya: Closing thread 12. :thumbsup:
